title: Virtualized hover collation and screenreader summarizer for dense time-series
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current time-series hover + tooltip system attempts to render per-point tooltips and live ARIA updates for high-frequency charts (hundreds to thousands of points). In practice this causes jank, excessive DOM churn, and noisy screen reader output. Users building dashboards with high-series-density lose both performance and useful semantic context.
tasks: Design a virtualized hover collation pattern that groups proximate points into a single summarized hover state for pointer interactions
Define an SR-friendly summarizer that emits stable, digestible announcements instead of raw per-point updates
Prototype a lightweight in-memory aggregation layer (component-level) to compute summary metrics for visible viewport windows
Create interactive specs in Figma showing collapsed hover states, collapsed legend rows, and accessible announcement examples
Run performance benchmarks comparing current per-point tooltip rendering vs. virtualized collation with 1k/10k point series
Write acceptance criteria and QA checklist for a11y engineers and SDEs
decisions: Use a viewport-level virtualizer: summarize points that fall within an X-pixel radius into one hover cluster
Tooltips for clustered items will present aggregate stats (min, max, median, sample count) plus an affordance to ‘expand details’ which triggers an out-of-band panel (not ARIA live) for full listing
Screen reader announcements will be throttled to at most one announcement per interaction focus change and will use a structured sentence template to reduce verbosity
We will prefer semantic DOM reduction (fewer nodes) over micro-animations when under SLO pressure to keep frame budget stable
tradeoffs: Cluster summaries reduce precision visible on hover — acceptable for dashboards where trend visibility is more important than individual sample inspection
Extra step to ‘expand details’ adds discoverability burden but keeps default experience performant and calm for SR users
Aggregation introduces slight latency in showing the most recent point on very fast-moving live charts; mitigated by tuning aggregation window and sampling policy
accessibility_considerations: ARIA: Use role=dialog for the expanded details panel; the collapsed summary will use aria-live='polite' with a concise template (series name, time range, count, primary metric)
Keyboard: Hover cluster must be reachable via keyboard focus; tabbing focuses nearest cluster and announces summary, with Enter to open expanded details
Screen reader ergonomics: Avoid streaming many announcements; provide explicit gesture/keyboard to inspect raw samples
WCAG: Ensure color/contrast for cluster markers and summary badges meets AA; provide non-color indicators for cluster size
performance_notes: Prototype uses a single ephemeral aggregation layer per chart instance to compute clustering in O(n) per viewport change; experiments show 3-4x reduction in DOM updates on 10k point series
Prefer Canvas-backed point grids for dense tracks; overlay minimal SVG/DOM for interactive hotspots to minimize paint cost
Throttle recalculation to animation frames and debounce viewport resizes by 90ms to avoid thrashing during fast panning
Batch ARIA updates: consolidate announcement string on the next RAF rather than streaming during micro-moves

acceptance_criteria: Hovering over dense series produces at most one tooltip DOM node per visible cluster
Screen reader announces concise summary for clusters and does not emit per-sample announcements during pointer move
Performance benchmarks show >=50% reduction in tooltip-related layout cost for 5k point series compared to baseline
Design handoff includes Figma specs, interaction states, copy for SR templates, and QA checklist
